npcs.name: Ferryman
npcs.line: The crossing is short. Shall I take you over to the other island?

npcs.name: Farmer
npcs.line: Good day. Mind the mud, it clings to boots.

nodes.line: There is always work on a farm.
Now that you mention it, aye.
You are a fine hand, I will say that.
Aye. The little ones are down with fever. Bring me six healing herbs.
Good green herbs. The village will sleep easier tonight.
Winter is coming. Bring me two health potions, and the barn is yours to call friend.
Fine brewing! You have my thanks again.
Aye, the rats are eating me out of house and home.
Fine tails! You have my thanks, and the village's.
The barley is up, but the rats are fat this year.
They eat my grain and leave their tails behind.
Dry for now. My knee says rain by the weekend.

npcs.name: Trader
npcs.line: Welcome, friend. Bread, cheese, and fair prices.

nodes.line: Slow days. The road is quiet and my cart is full.
Folk stay home when the wolves howl at night.

npcs.name: House agent
npcs.line: Welcome home. Rent is taken from the gold in your depot each month; after a few days of reminders an unpaid house is lost. What shall I see to?

nodes.line: It is done. Take a look.
The house is no longer yours. Farewell.
Take a seat when you are by the boat. It leaves in {departure}.
Next departure in {departure}. Do not be late.

npcs.name: Smith
npcs.line: Bring me two of a kind and some coins, and I will make one better piece of them.

npcs.name: Thomas
npcs.line: Good to see you, my child. Mind the mud, it clings to boots.

choices.text: How do I fight a beast?
What of the old root cellar?

nodes.line: The old root cellar in the south-west is overrun with burrow rats, and it is dark down there. Someone must thin them.

choices.text: I have the six burrow tails.

nodes.line: Take the stairs in the lane south-west of our house and mind the dark; a torch may lie in a chest near the foot. Bring me six burrow tails.
Six tails, and the cellar is quiet again. Keep these torches, you will need them below.
The cellar is quiet. There are deeper holes on this island, though.
Walk up to the beast and strike until it falls. Back away and eat or drink when it bites hard.
Open the corpse and take what it carried into your backpack. A fresh corpse may be skinned, too.
Work? There is always some on a farm.

choices.text: I have the five rat tails.
About the rats in the granary...

nodes.line: There are rats in the granary, more than ever, and they come down from the north. Bring me five rat tails and I will count them.
That is a fair count. The beasts are fleeing something in the north, I fear.
They keep coming down from the north. Something is wrong up there.

npcs.name: Martha
npcs.line: Come in, my dear, the kettle is on.

nodes.line: Healing herbs grow in the meadow to the east, and they grow back. Pick only what you need.

choices.text: And how do I brew them?

nodes.line: Use my table with three healing herbs in your backpack, and a health potion comes of them. Keep one in your quick slot for a bad moment.
I may need a hand when the time is right.
The animals flee from the north, and frightened folk fall ill. Brew me a health potion at my table.
Well brewed, my dear. Take these for the road.
They say something on Watch Hill has stirred. I do not like it.

npcs.name: Hanna
npcs.line: Hello! I know where everybody is.

nodes.line: Do you mean home, the town, or the places outside it?
Mother is in the kitchen, and father is in the barn or the fields. Grandfather is at the pier by day.
Brother Anselm lives in the chapel, north of the green. The reeve is across the High Street from the green, east of the chapel. The storehouse is west of the green.
Helen sells at her stall on the green and lives by Pier Street. Agnes weaves in her house across the square; Jacob works at the smithy and lives beside it.
Simon has a hut by Fir Wood in the north-west. The quarry is in the north-east, and the herb meadow to the east.

npcs.name: Old Victor
npcs.line: There you are, child. The old boat still floats, and so do I.

choices.text: I am ready to leave the island.

nodes.line: The sea is wide and I row it only once. My boat needs mending first; come back when you are level 8 and we shall see.
I rowed the north shore when I was young. The hill was quiet then.
The keel of my boat is rotten, and I must mend it before I can sail on. Come back to me later.

choices.text: The boat is mended, take me across.

nodes.line: I am too old to row back, mind. Whoever crosses cannot return, for the island is closed behind you.

choices.text: I will stay a while longer.

npcs.name: Agnes
npcs.line: Welcome, child. Mind the loom, the thread tangles.

choices.text: How do I skin a corpse?

nodes.line: My loom is hungry for silk. The cave spiders in the Old Mine spin the finest there is.
Bring me four skeins of spider silk from the Old Mine under the quarry. Go with a light, for they bite from the dark.
Soft and strong, just as I hoped. Here is a cap for your trouble.
The new cloth is already on the loom.
Use a fresh corpse and you take its hide, but only while it is fresh. A rat hide is small, yet four make a jerkin.

choices.text: Will you buy hides and pelts?

nodes.line: Use my loom with four rat hides in your backpack and a hide jerkin comes of them. Wear it, and bites hurt less.
There is always cloth to mend.
The wind off the hill came early and cold. Make me a hide jerkin at my loom, from four rat hides.
A warm, sound jerkin. Simon says the boars are tearing up Fir Wood; they flee the hill, too.
The wind off Watch Hill is cold and strange.

npcs.name: Helen
npcs.line: Welcome, child. Bread, cheese, and fair prices.

nodes.line: Tails, tusks, hides and pelts, spider silk and goblin ears, and fresh rat corpses. My purse is thin, so come back when it has filled.

npcs.name: Simon
npcs.line: Hail, child. Fir Wood is quiet today, mostly.

nodes.line: Bears have denned in a hollow under the north-west edge of the wood, and they grow bold. I split my logs with wedges made of their claws.
Go down by the hut path into the hollow, and bring me three bear claws. A bear bites hard, so go well fed.
Three fine claws. Take these trousers; thorns will not tear them.
The wood is quieter now. The bears will be back, as bears are.
Use a fir tree and you take a log; the tree grows back in time. The more you cut, the better you cut.
The smith needs them at his forge, and the joiner for his planks. Fire eats them, too.
The wood is never done.

choices.text: I have the four boar tusks.

nodes.line: Boars from the hill are tearing up my firs. Bring me four of their tusks.
Four good tusks. They did not come for the acorns; something drove them.
Jacob is worried about the old gate. Go and see him.

npcs.name: Jacob
npcs.line: Come in, child. Bring me two of a kind and some coins, and I will make one better piece of them.

nodes.line: Use an iron ore rock in the quarry and you take ore; the rock grows back in time. Wolves roam there, so go ready.
Use my forge with three iron ore and two logs in your backpack and an iron shield comes of them. Two equal pieces and coins, and I merge them into one better.

choices.text: Do you buy anything from the hunt?

nodes.line: The forge is never idle.
The hill road needs a gate that holds. Forge me an iron shield, and mind the wolves at the quarry.
Heavy and true. Take this plank shield for it; I have made it a little better.
The gate will hold, I think. Brother Anselm is worried about the ruin.

npcs.name: Nicholas
npcs.line: Good day, child. I keep the book of the houses and the rent.

choices.text: How do I buy a house?

nodes.line: My old rent ledger was lost in the Old Mine under the quarry, and the roll cannot be mended without it. It lies in a chest at the far end, they say.
Take a light into the mine and search its far end. Bring me the ledger, and I will pay you well.
My ledger, a little damp but whole. Take this vest, and my thanks.
Goblins have dug in beyond the mine, and they rob the carts. The reeve pays for their ears.
The warren lies below the mine; follow the stairs at its far end. Bring me six goblin ears.
Six ears, counted twice. Take this shield and your pay.
The carts roll safer now. The reeve does not forget.
Find a house with a sign for sale, stand before it and use the sign. The price is taken from your backpack.
A house has a chest to keep things in and a bed to rest in. The rent falls due each month, and a house left unpaid is lost.
The storehouse has six chests, and each one opens your own depot, whichever you choose. What you leave there is yours in any town.

npcs.name: Brother Anselm
npcs.line: Peace, child. The chapel is open to all.

nodes.line: Beneath the ruin lies an old barrow, and its dead walk again. I would lay them to rest, but I need what they leave behind.
The stairs are inside the ruin on Watch Hill. Bring me five handfuls of bone dust, and I will lay it in the chapel ground.
The dust will rest in hallowed ground. Take this cap, child, and my blessing.
The barrow is quieter, and the dead rest easier.
Here you rest, and here you wake if you fall in the wild. A fall costs you, so be careful.

choices.text: Do you take what the dead leave?

nodes.line: There may be a task for the ready.

choices.text: I have a shard of the warden.

nodes.line: Something in the ruin on Watch Hill has stirred, and a stone warden guards it. Bring me a shard of it, that I may learn what wakes.
A cold shard of old stone. The hill only kept its watch; take this charm.
Old Victor waits at the pier, when you are ready to leave.

npcs.name: Edda
npcs.line: Few climb this far. The mountain keeps its own counsel, and so do I.

nodes.line: Crown Crag, the old watch of the isle. Beasts and worse live on it and beneath it.
I have little use for visitors, but I can use a strong arm.
Wargs hunt on the slopes above, and they thin my herd of goats. Bring me four of their fangs.
Sharp and clean. Take this cap, and a little coin.
The wargs were only the start. A stone maze lies beneath the isle, and horned guards walk it.

choices.text: What would you have me do?

nodes.line: The maze lies under the mine and the warren, at the end of the deep stairs. Bring me three fragments of the guards' horned helms.
So they are real. These trousers should serve you better than they served me.
The guards serve something that sits at the top of the crag. It wears a cairn of stones for a crown.
Climb the stairs at the foot of the crag, past the wargs, to the summit. Bring me the seal it carries, and be ready to fall back.
The seal, and you walk back down on your own feet. Keep this vest and the coin; you have earned both.
The crag is quiet for now. Such things grow back, in time.
